Pokémon companion credits

Models supplied by Lakshya. The creators and licences below come from their embedded source credits. Pokémon characters and names belong to their respective rights holders; this prototype claims no official affiliation.

Vaporeon

Vaporeon by nguyenlouis32 (https://sketchfab.com/nguyenlouis32).

CC-BY-4.0 (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

Original model geometry, textures and rig retained. Procedural poses and garden placement were added for this prototype.

Articuno

Articuno by nguyenlouis32 (https://sketchfab.com/nguyenlouis32).

CC-BY-4.0 (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

Original model geometry, textures and rig retained. Procedural poses and garden placement were added for this prototype.

Pikachu

Pikachu by gaddiellartey2010 (https://sketchfab.com/gaddiellartey2010).

CC-BY-4.0 (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

The selected small source file is retained unchanged. A procedural quadruped rig, body tessellation and two rounded forepaw pads are created at runtime; original textures and UVs are retained. Procedural poses and garden placement were added for this prototype.

Bulbasaur

Bulbasaur by kishi (https://sketchfab.com/ash.takafumi).

CC-BY-4.0 (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

Geometry simplified; source vertex colours retained. A procedural quadruped rig was added. Procedural poses and garden placement were added for this prototype.

Charmander

Charmander by JavierCarmona (https://sketchfab.com/JavierCarmona).

CC-BY-4.0 (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

The replacement model was simplified, an unused mesh removed, and its tail-flame material corrected. Selected source positions, UVs and original image bytes were retained. A two-legged procedural rig is added at runtime. Procedural poses and garden placement were added for this prototype.

Charizard

Charizard by nguyenlouis32 (https://sketchfab.com/nguyenlouis32).

CC-BY-4.0 (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

Original model geometry, textures and rig retained. Orange skin is selectively deepened at runtime to match the supplied Charmander, while cream and teal areas retain their source colours. The exported black-and-white flame masks receive a warm transparent flame material at runtime; the original source file is unchanged. Procedural poses and garden placement were added for this prototype.

Snorlax

Snorlax Pokemon by OWL (https://sketchfab.com/owl06).

CC-BY-4.0 (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

The model was simplified and legacy materials converted while retaining selected source positions, UVs and image bytes. A procedural sleeping pose, breathing and vector ZZZ markers are added at runtime. Procedural poses and garden placement were added for this prototype.

Oak’s laboratory and garden Poké Balls

Pokemon Professor Oak by 3D Resource (https://sketchfab.com/lopuh22721). CC-BY-4.0 (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

Pokeballs 1-st Pack by DoubleTrouble (https://sketchfab.com/AJLENb). CC-BY-4.0 (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

Set of 4 Pokéballs by damien_max59 (https://sketchfab.com/damienbouchez59). CC-BY-4.0 (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

Oak’s static model was deduplicated, its legacy materials converted, and sleeves and hands lowered in a separate baked pose. No skeleton, voice or character animation was supplied. All ten supplied Poké Ball variants were normalized and selectively simplified; constant source colors were baked into vertex colors, and source gloss and emission were adapted to one shared outdoor material. Garden placements share geometry and materials. The laboratory scenery is an original lightweight interpretation of the visual references, not geometry extracted from a viewer.

Recorded calls

Four short Pikachu, Bulbasaur, Charmander and Charizard recordings come from the visible Anime Cry players on Psypoke. That source identifies anime calls separately from game cries, but does not document their dub language or episode; these are not certified Japanese recordings. Exact source records accompany the files. Articuno and Vaporeon retain the game cries described below. Snorlax is silent.

Existing recordings retrieved through PokéAPI’s cries repository, which credits Pokémon Showdown, Veekun and Sounds Resource. They are community-hosted game audio, not newly generated voices. Repository availability does not establish permission for a public commercial release.

Nearby calls are enabled by the explicit Let’s start action, unless a saved mute preference is present. Recordings download lazily on a nearby encounter or greeting. Guide can mute them at any time.

The credits above describe the distributed adaptations. Original source files and detailed preparation records are retained separately; public attribution accompanies the portfolio.
